clippings.speaker: Walter Matthau
clippings.quote: How could you not be friendly with him? This man is amenable, delightful... Generous, no ego problem. He has no ego problem. This man is without an ego.
clippings.title: Encore Presentation: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau: Great Friends and Costars
clippings.context: Joint Larry King interview recorded July 3, 1997 while promoting Out to Sea, rebroadcast June 30, 2001; Matthau's reply is split across two of King's prompts.

clippings.speaker: Walter Matthau
clippings.quote: No, he's the perfectionist and I'm not, and we never clash.
clippings.title: Encore Presentation: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau: Great Friends and Costars
clippings.context: Same 1997 joint Larry King interview, when King asked which of them was the perfectionist.

clippings.speaker: Walter Matthau
clippings.quote: Yes, I think the magic is that he's neat and nifty and I'm slow and sloppy.
clippings.title: Encore Presentation: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau: Great Friends and Costars
clippings.context: Asked in the 1997 joint interview whether they sensed it was working right away on The Fortune Cookie; he then joked the reverse is true in real life.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: we're on the same wave length when we work, obviously. We seem to think the same in comedy. In other words, what I think may be funny, Walter will probably think will be funny.
clippings.title: Encore Presentation: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau: Great Friends and Costars
clippings.context: Lemmon's answer when King asked what the magic between them was, in the 1997 joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: When we get on that set, he's there. He's cold with the lines. I mean, he knows them cold and we're set and we go. And he's knocking it out from take one on or from the first read through.
clippings.title: Encore Presentation: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau: Great Friends and Costars
clippings.context: Lemmon pushing back on Matthau's self-effacing claim that he wasn't a perfectionist, 1997 joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: Totally. It was like sitting down, as Carol was intimating I think. No acting showed. He would be the character, and he wasn't the same all the time.
clippings.title: Remembering Walter Matthau
clippings.context: Larry King tribute two weeks after Matthau's death, asked whether his rapport with Matthau came naturally.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: Walter was nominated for best actor: not because of my direction, because I shut my mouth up and let him alone.
clippings.title: Remembering Walter Matthau
clippings.context: Same 2000 tribute, showing a set photo from Kotch, which Lemmon directed.

notes: All from two CNN Larry King transcripts (1997 joint interview, 2000 tribute); Tampa Bay Times archive paywalled, RogerEbert.com 403.
